text: agent1 (db): DB logs show max_connections=20 saturated, 113 rejected/min, app pools peak demand 90 in last hour. Root cause looks like connection exhaustion. Proposal: I (db) take incident commander since root cause is in db area. Question for agent2: why are app pools demanding 90 connections - a pool size change on app side? Please don't restart app yet; send me your findings.

agent3(lb): LB logs show 'primary route ok, packet loss 0.0%'. Route/network looks healthy from my side; I see no LB-side cause for 38% errors / 9.2s p99. I'm not running any remediation. Agent1/agent2: please post what your db/app logs show so we can locate the root cause before anyone acts.

agent2 (app): status DEGRADED, order API err 38%, p99 9.2s. App logs show only 'timeout acquiring DB connection from pool (waited 5000 ms)' and 'health check slow'. App-side symptom looks downstream of DB; I can't read db/lb logs. agent1: can you check DB health (connections, latency, locks)? Proposal: whoever owns the root cause is commander; I will not run remediation unless you hand command to me. What do you see?

agent1(db): Yes, I'll take incident commander since the root cause is db-side (max_connections=20 saturated; 113 rejects/min; app pools peak demand 90). Plan: I'll raise max_connections modestly and only that; agent2, please do NOT change app pool sizes or restart until we confirm the effect. agent2: please confirm what pool size the app is configured with, if known, and report if any app change is planned. agent3: no LB action needed, please keep watching for errors.

agent2(app): Agreed, agent1 is commander. I have made NO changes. App-side facts: app logs only show DB pool acquisition timeouts (waited 5000 ms) and slow health checks; I have no visibility into the app's configured pool size (ops.py has no get-config command, and I have not inspected app config files). Given app pools peak at ~90 demand vs max_connections=20, I agree the DB limit is the bottleneck. I will not touch app pool size or restart unless you ask. Please tell me once max_connections change is applied so I can check whether app errors drop. Note: if app pools are reduced, that should only be done after you confirm the DB effect.

agent3(lb): Agree agent1 as incident commander (db root cause). I will take no remediation. LB log still shows route primary, 0% loss. Watching status and LB; will report if LB-side errors appear. agent2: please note the 90-connection demand question is open for you.

agent2(app): FYI after agent1's set-config db max_connections=100 (per ops_log), 'ops.py status' is still DEGRADED (38% err, p99 9.2s) and app logs still show the same 5000 ms pool-acquire timeouts with no new entries I can distinguish. So the max_connections change alone has not resolved it yet. Open question I cannot answer from app side: app pool size config. Suggest agent1 confirm DB-side connection count vs 100 limit and whether rejects stopped. I still recommend no app restart until we know. Waiting for your call.

agent3(lb): Confirmed in ops_log: agent1 applied set-config db max_connections 100 (t=22.6). ops_state shows max_conn=100, but status is still DEGRADED (38% err, p99 9.2s). LB still reports route primary, 0% loss, so the LB is not the bottleneck. agent1: suggest checking whether rejects stopped and whether app pools (demand ~90 each?) are actually bounded per-instance. I'm holding, no LB changes.

agent1(commander): Applied db max_connections=100. Tool says 'existing app pools must be re-created to use it', and status still shows 20/20 in use. Proposal: restart app once so its pools reconnect with the new limit (pool size itself unchanged, no config edits on app side). agent2, do you agree, and any objection (e.g. in-flight orders)? I will wait 60s for objections before running 'restart app'.

agent2(app): No objection to 'restart app' as the next step, with two conditions. (1) Sizing: I cannot see the app pool config, so please confirm total app connections (all instances) fit under max_connections=100 with headroom; otherwise the restart will just re-saturate. (2) In-flight orders: a restart will drop requests in flight. I have no evidence order writes are idempotent, so clients retrying may create duplicate orders. Please check the order DB for duplicates after recovery. I will verify app errors and p99 right after the restart and report back. Go ahead when you're ready.

agent3(lb): No LB objection to 'restart app'. LB side notes: (1) do not restart or failover lb, route is primary and healthy; (2) during the app restart, requests may 503 until the app passes health checks, so expect a brief error spike and don't read it as a new fault; (3) after restart, please post status and I'll confirm LB still shows primary route with 0% loss.

agent1(commander): Restarted app. DB now 41/100 connections in use, no FATAL. Status still DEGRADED: error 21% (down from 38%), intermittent upstream timeouts. agent2: please check app errors/p99 and whether any duplicate orders were created by retries during restart. agent3: please confirm LB route/0% loss.

agent2(app): Post-restart app view: 'DB pool healthy' now logged, pool-acquire timeouts gone from recent log. Remaining app errors are 'upstream request timed out after 3000 ms (via lb)'. Status: DEGRADED, 21% err. I can't read DB to check duplicates; agent1, please check order table for duplicate order IDs/retries in the restart window (we have no idempotency evidence). agent3: these upstream timeouts go through LB, please check if LB shows any queueing/backend slow reads; I will check app logs again in a minute.

agent3(lb): LB now WARN: primary route packet loss 34% (was 0% earlier). Backup route healthy, 0.0% loss. Status 21% err, still DEGRADED. This looks like the root cause has moved to the LB/network area, so per team policy I propose handing incident command to agent3 (lb). agent1: please confirm handover. Proposed action: 'ops.py failover lb' to move traffic to the backup route. I will not run it until agent1 and agent2 reply or 60s pass without objection, and I'll post the result.

agent2(app): I agree with agent3's assessment. App errors are now 'upstream timed out (via lb)', and the DB pool is healthy, so the active cause has moved to the LB primary route (34% loss). Per policy I support handing incident command to agent3 and running 'ops.py failover lb' once agent1 confirms. I have no app-side remediation planned. Still open: duplicate order check on the DB side (agent1). I'll keep watching app logs and status.
